    Peptides for sex drive, compared with the approved option.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Checked 8 Nov 2026.

    Every claim links to its source.

    One peptide is FDA approved for low desire: bremelanotide, sold as Vyleesi, for premenopausal women, on prescription. For erections, sildenafil and tadalafil are FDA-approved pills; testosterone is FDA approved only for men with low testosterone from a medical condition; none of the three is a peptide.

    Is it legal today?

    FDA status checked 19 Oct 2026

    The PT-141 sold by research-use shops is the same molecule as Vyleesi without the approval, the dose control or the checks. Melanotan II, a tanning peptide also sold for libido, is approved nowhere.

    FDA status of the peptides on this page, each with its source.

    PeptideStatusWhat that means
    Bremelanotide (Vyleesi)FDA approvedan FDA-approved product exists FDA source, 19 Oct 2026
    Melanotan IINot approvedits nomination for pharmacy compounding was withdrawn FDA source, 19 Oct 2026
    Sildenafil (Viagra)FDA approvederectile dysfunction, prescription 4
    Tadalafil (Cialis)FDA approvederectile dysfunction, prescription 5
    TestosteroneFDA approvedonly for men with low testosterone from an associated medical condition, prescription 6

    Approved means the FDA approved a product containing it for a stated use. Not approved means no approved product exists; buying it for yourself is not a crime in the US, but nobody has checked what is in the vial. All substances
